claim:
Let \(X\) be a compact metric space, \(f:X	o X\) a measurable map, and \(\mu\) a probability measure. Assume Berger's second metric emergence has finite small-scale value \(N:=\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\mathscr E'_\mu(f)(\varepsilon)\in\{2,3,\ldots\}\). Let \(
u_1,\ldots,
u_N\) be the distinct empirical limits whose basins cover \(\mu\)-almost every point, and put \(p_i=\mu(B(
u_i))\). Then every \(p_i>0\), the system is empirical, and \(\mathscr E_\mu(f)=\mathscr E'_\mu(f)\). If \(d_W\) is the Kantorovich-Wasserstein distance and \[\Delta:=\min_{1\le i<j\le N}\min\{p_i,p_j\}d_W(
u_i,
u_j),\] then \(\Delta>0\), and the common metric emergence equals \(N\) for every \(0<\varepsilon\le\Delta\), while it is at most \(N-1\) for every \(\varepsilon>\Delta\). Thus \(\Delta\) is the exact first resolution at which the \(N\) asymptotic statistics can be compressed to fewer than \(N\) prototypes.
integrity: The proof is analytic and self-contained once the cited emergence-to-quantization results are accepted; no numerical experiment or external certificate is used.
scientific_limitations: The formula identifies only the first drop from \(N\) prototypes; lower prototype counts are general weighted \(k\)-median problems.
The theorem is for the average-distance/Kantorovich-Wasserstein emergence used in the motivating source.
A folklore occurrence of the elementary finite-metric lemma in broad quantization or facility-location literature cannot be excluded by the searches performed.
title: The exact first breakpoint of finite metric emergence
